Bugs fixed after ipw 1.3.2

Source: vignettes/articles/bug-fixes.Rmd
bug-fixes.Rmd

This page describes the bugs that were found in a review of ipw after version 1.3.2 and fixed in the next version. For each bug it shows a small example and runs it in three versions:

  • ipw 1.2.1.1, the last version before the 1.3 rewrite;
  • ipw 1.3.2, the version on CRAN when the review was done;
  • this version, the one this page was built with.

The weights of each version are compared with the correct weights, which are computed by hand on this page with glm(), MASS::polr() or survival::coxph(), without using ipw. A difference of about 1e-15 is rounding; a difference of 0.1 means that some weights are off by 10%.

The results of 1.2.1.1 and 1.3.2 were made once in separate R sessions with the script data-raw/make-bugfix-article-data.R and are stored with this article; the correct weights and the results of this version are computed every time the page is built.

Who is affected?

You are affected if you used one of the following with an older version. The sections below explain each case; the table at the end summarises them.

  • an offset() term in a model formula (1.3.1 and 1.3.2);
  • denominator = ~ . (1.3.1 and 1.3.2: an error, so no wrong results);
  • a 0/1 exposure stored as a factor, with the level "1" first (all older versions);
  • an ordinal exposure stored as text (1.3.1 and 1.3.2; 1.2.1.1 stopped with an unclear error), or as a factor whose levels are in alphabetical rather than dose order (all older versions);
  • ipwtm() with family = "survival" and type = "first" or "cens", where subjects have their own visit times (all older versions);
  • ipwtm() with a covariate that is called selvar (1.3.1 and 1.3.2);
  • ipwtm() with id/timevar combinations that occur more than once (all older versions);
  • ipwtm() with family = "survival" and the ties argument (all older versions).

1. offset() terms were dropped (1.3.1 and 1.3.2)

An offset is a term with a fixed coefficient of 1, for example the log of follow-up time when the chance of exposure grows with time at risk. In ipw 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 the model formula was rebuilt from its term labels, and R does not count offset() as a term label, so the offset was silently left out: the model was fitted as a ~ l.

cases$offset$call
#> ipwpoint(exposure = a, family = "binomial", link = "logit", denominator = ~l + 
#>     offset(off), data = data)

The correct weights, by hand:

d <- cases$offset$data
p <- fitted(glm(a ~ l + offset(off), family = binomial, data = d))
ref_offset <- unname(1 / ifelse(d$a == 1, p, 1 - p))
Version Result Largest relative difference from the correct weights
1.2.1.1 Weights 0
1.3.2 (CRAN) Weights 1.1
this version (1.3.2.9000) Weights 0

Fix: the model formula is now used exactly as written.

2. denominator = ~ . failed (1.3.1 and 1.3.2)

~ . means “all other columns of data”. In 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 the check for missing variables looked for a column called . and stopped.

cases$dot$call
#> ipwpoint(exposure = a, family = "binomial", link = "logit", denominator = ~., 
#>     data = data)
names(cases$dot$data)
#> [1] "l1" "l2" "a"
d <- cases$dot$data
p <- fitted(glm(a ~ l1 + l2, family = binomial, data = d))
ref_dot <- unname(1 / ifelse(d$a == 1, p, 1 - p))
Version Result Largest relative difference from the correct weights
1.2.1.1 Weights 0
1.3.2 (CRAN) Error: Variables not found in data: .
this version (1.3.2.9000) Weights 0

Fix: ~ . works again in ipwpoint(). In ipwtm() it is now a clear error, because the dot would also include the id, time and exposure columns; list the covariates there.

3. A factor exposure with levels c("1", "0") swapped the probabilities

For a binomial exposure, ipw checked that the values were 0 and 1, but a factor with those labels passed the check. glm() then models the probability of the second level. With levels in the order "1", "0" that is the probability of being unexposed, so every exposed subject got the weight meant for an unexposed one and vice versa. Factors with levels "0", "1" (the default order) were fine.

cases$factor$call
#> ipwpoint(exposure = a, family = "binomial", link = "logit", denominator = ~l1 + 
#>     l2, data = data)
levels(cases$factor$data$a)
#> [1] "1" "0"
d <- cases$factor$data
p <- fitted(glm(a_num ~ l1 + l2, family = binomial, data = d))
ref_factor <- unname(1 / ifelse(d$a_num == 1, p, 1 - p))
Version Result Largest relative difference from the correct weights
1.2.1.1 Weights 8.7
1.3.2 (CRAN) Weights 8.7
this version (1.3.2.9000) Weights 0

Fix: a 0/1 exposure stored as a factor or text is converted by its labels, so the order of the levels no longer matters.

4. An ordinal exposure given as text was ordered alphabetically (1.3.1 and 1.3.2)

For family = "ordinal" the exposure is turned into a factor. Text is then sorted alphabetically, so "low", "mid", "high" became "high" < "low" < "mid", and in 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 the ordinal model was fitted with the wrong order without any message. ipw 1.2.1.1 stopped with an error that did not say what was wrong. The same alphabetical order is used in every version for an unordered factor with text levels, unless its levels were set in dose order.

cases$ordinal$call
#> ipwpoint(exposure = dose, family = "ordinal", link = "logit", 
#>     denominator = ~l, data = data)
table(cases$ordinal$data$dose)
#> 
#> high  low  mid 
#>  146  193  161

The correct weights use the dose order:

d <- cases$ordinal$data
d$dose_ord <- factor(d$dose, levels = c("low", "mid", "high"), ordered = TRUE)
fit <- MASS::polr(dose_ord ~ l, data = d, method = "logistic")
pr <- predict(fit, type = "probs")
ref_ordinal <- unname(1 / pr[cbind(seq_len(nrow(d)), as.integer(d$dose_ord))])
Version Result Largest relative difference from the correct weights
1.2.1.1 Error: replacement has 0 rows, data has 500
1.3.2 (CRAN) Weights 1.8
this version (1.3.2.9000) Error: Ordinal exposure is a character vector, whose order is not defined (it would be sorted alphabetically). Use an…

Fix: a text exposure is now an error that asks for an ordered factor or numeric codes, and an unordered factor whose levels are not numbers gives a warning. With an ordered factor the weights are correct in all versions:

w <- ipwpoint(exposure = dose_ord, family = "ordinal", link = "logit",
              denominator = ~ l, data = d)
max_rel(w$ipw.weights, ref_ordinal)
#> [1] 0

5. Survival exposure: subjects with their own visit times

For family = "survival" with type = "first" (and the censoring weights with type = "cens"), each row covers an interval (tstart, timevar], and its probability should use the baseline hazard over that interval. Older versions used the increase in the baseline hazard since the previous time point in the whole data set. That is the same thing when all subjects are seen at the same times, as in haartdat, but not when they have their own visit times: the hazard of a row was then only counted from the last visit of any subject, so it was too small.

cases$survival$call
#> ipwtm(exposure = a, family = "survival", denominator = ~l, id = id, 
#>     tstart = tstart, timevar = time, type = "first", data = data)
head(cases$survival$data[, c("id", "tstart", "time", "a", "l")], 4)
#>   id tstart time a          l
#> 1  1      0    5 0  1.3774531
#> 2  1      5   14 0  0.1963246
#> 3  1     14   28 1 -0.2319014
#> 4  2      0   13 0  0.9947626

The correct weights use the cumulative baseline hazard H at both ends of each row’s interval:

d <- cases$survival$data
fit <- coxph(Surv(tstart, time, a) ~ l, data = d)
bh <- basehaz(fit, centered = TRUE)
H <- function(t) {
  h <- approx(bh$time, bh$hazard, xout = t, method = "constant", rule = 2)$y
  h[t < min(bh$time)] <- 0
  h
}
haz <- (H(d$time) - H(d$tstart)) * predict(fit, type = "risk")
p_obs <- ifelse(d$a == 1, 1 - exp(-haz), exp(-haz))
ref_survival <- unname(ave(1 / p_obs, d$id, FUN = cumprod))

(The package tests also check this against a baseline hazard computed from the risk sets by hand, without basehaz().)

Version Result Largest relative difference from the correct weights
1.2.1.1 Weights 25
1.3.2 (CRAN) Weights 25
this version (1.3.2.9000) Weights 4.4e-16

With a common time grid, as in haartdat, nothing changes: all versions give the same weights.

Fix: each row now uses the hazard over its own interval, as type = "all" already did. The article Survival weights with individual visit times describes this bug in detail: every version from ipw 1.0 to 1.3.2 is affected, and it shows the old and the new code.

6. A covariate called selvar was overwritten (ipwtm(), 1.3.1 and 1.3.2)

From version 1.3.1, ipwtm() adds a column called selvar to the data to mark the rows that enter the exposure model. A covariate of the user with that name was overwritten, so the model used the indicator instead.

cases$selvar$call
#> ipwtm(exposure = a, family = "binomial", link = "logit", denominator = ~l + 
#>     selvar, id = id, timevar = time, type = "first", data = data)

By hand: the rows up to and including the first exposure enter the model, and the weights are cumulative products within subject.

d <- cases$selvar$data
sel <- ave(d$a, d$id, FUN = function(x) cumsum(cumsum(x)) <= 1) == 1
p <- rep(1, nrow(d))
p[sel] <- fitted(glm(a ~ l + selvar, family = binomial, data = d[sel, ]))
p_obs <- ifelse(!sel, 1, ifelse(d$a == 1, p, 1 - p))
ref_selvar <- unname(ave(1 / p_obs, d$id, FUN = cumprod))
Version Result Largest relative difference from the correct weights
1.2.1.1 Weights 4.4e-16
1.3.2 (CRAN) Weights 3.6
this version (1.3.2.9000) Weights 4.4e-16

Fix: the internal column now has a name that does not clash (.ipw_selvar); the selvar element of the result is unchanged.

7. Duplicated id/timevar rows were accepted (ipwtm())

If the same subject and time occur twice, for example after a faulty merge, the cumulative product is taken over both copies in an arbitrary order and the weights are wrong. ipwtm() accepted such data without a message (ipwprobtm() already refused it).

d <- cases$duplicates$data
sum(duplicated(d[, c("id", "time")]))
#> [1] 3
Version Result Largest relative difference from the correct weights
1.2.1.1 Weights
1.3.2 (CRAN) Weights
this version (1.3.2.9000) Error: Each combination of ‘id’ and ‘timevar’ must occur only once.

Fix: duplicated id/timevar combinations are now an error.

8. The ties argument was ignored (ipwtm(), survival)

Arguments in ... are passed to the model function. For family = "survival" the Cox model always used Efron’s method for tied times, so ties = "breslow" had no effect, in 1.2.1.1 as well as in 1.3.x.

cases$ties$call
#> ipwtm(exposure = haartind, family = "survival", numerator = ~sex + 
#>     age, denominator = ~sex + age + cd4.sqrt, id = patient, tstart = tstart, 
#>     timevar = fuptime, type = "first", data = data, ties = "breslow")

By hand, with Breslow’s method for both models:

d <- haartdat
sel <- ave(d$haartind, d$patient, FUN = function(x) cumsum(cumsum(x)) <= 1) == 1
p_breslow <- function(rhs) {
  f <- update(rhs, Surv(tstart, fuptime, haartind) ~ .)
  fit <- coxph(f, data = d[sel, ], ties = "breslow")
  bh <- basehaz(fit, centered = TRUE)
  H <- function(t) {
    h <- approx(bh$time, bh$hazard, xout = t, method = "constant", rule = 2)$y
    h[t < min(bh$time)] <- 0
    h
  }
  p <- rep(1, nrow(d))
  haz <- (H(d$fuptime[sel]) - H(d$tstart[sel])) * predict(fit, type = "risk")
  p[sel] <- ifelse(d$haartind[sel] == 1, 1 - exp(-haz), exp(-haz))
  p
}
ref_ties <- unname(ave(p_breslow(~ sex + age) / p_breslow(~ sex + age + cd4.sqrt),
                       d$patient, FUN = cumprod))
Version Result Largest relative difference from the correct weights
1.2.1.1 Weights 0.064
1.3.2 (CRAN) Weights 0.064
this version (1.3.2.9000) Weights 1.1e-15

Fix: ties is passed on to coxph(); the default is still Efron.

Summary

Case 1.2.1.1 1.3.2 (CRAN) this version (1.3.2.9000)
1. offset() in a formula correct wrong (up to 1.1) correct
2. denominator = ~ . correct error (should work) correct
3. factor exposure, levels “1”, “0” wrong (up to 8.7) wrong (up to 8.7) correct
4. ordinal exposure as text error (unclear message) wrong (up to 1.8) error, as it should
5. survival, own visit times wrong (up to 25) wrong (up to 25) correct
6. covariate called selvar correct wrong (up to 3.6) correct
7. duplicated id/timevar rows wrong (no error) wrong (no error) error, as it should
8. ties = “breslow” wrong (up to 0.064) wrong (up to 0.064) correct

All fixes are listed in the NEWS. The package tests (tests/testthat/test-audit*.R, test-regression*.R) check each case, and test-regression.R checks that, apart from these fixes, the weights are the same as in ipw 1.2.1.1 for 44 settings.
